status: PROPOSAL (Adhi, compute science). Hemanath freezes prices and budget in protocol.md at code freeze.

night2.assumptions: 346 held-out items x 4 conditions x 3 seeds; 11.0 h x 1 GPU worker(s), 70% of it planned for

rules: GPU tiers: median GPU-seconds in units, never below the floor
cached_lookup: the floor (caching never makes a condition cheaper)
decomposition_reeval: two MP reaction evaluations (2 x floor) plus any measured GPU time
budget per pair: one escalation path (cached_lookup + single_point + bounded_relaxation + decomposition_reeval)
second budget level: only if a full second main run also fits Night 2
notes: Measured on the GB10 after the phase-set and relaxation fixes (commit d4f012d; results/gb10/profile_s0_fix.json); replaces the earlier proposal, whose relaxation price was inflated by solid O2 failing to converge in every pair.

Relaxations: 13 of 20 dev pairs converged in that run; a later gas-molecule fix (376cde2) also converged 2 of the 3 BaO2 pairs. The rest are honest not_converged (hydrated oxalate, ammonium phosphates, a barium superoxide product).

Capacity: with the result cache (identical calculations computed once, every request still charged in full) each pair needs at most one real calculation per tier: 346 x mean(0.7 s single point + 44.2 s relaxation) = 4.3 GPU-hours expected, within 7.7 usable on one GB10. The p90 figure assumes every pair is as slow as the slowest tenth and is an upper bound.
Gemini calls, not the GPU, are the likely wall-clock limit overnight: set from the 7 PM dry run.
